subject.title: iOS app: node requests re-approval on every reconnect (token persistence bug)

question: Should the remaining iOS fix normalize volatile permission/status fields out of node approval requests, or should gateway reapproval continue to treat every iOS permission/status change as authorization drift?
rationale: Both choices affect the security boundary for approved node capabilities, and the current evidence only proves the QR bootstrap-token subset, not the repeated reapproval loop after manual and QR setup.

options.title: Stabilize iOS approval declarations
options.body: Keep reapproval for real new commands/capabilities while removing or normalizing volatile fields such as reachability/status from the approved node surface, with real iPhone reconnect proof.

options.title: Relax gateway permission drift handling
options.body: Change core reconciliation so permission downgrades or selected permission-status changes do not create reapproval, but require broader gateway security review and regression coverage.

options.title: Close after current-main live proof
options.body: If maintainers can prove current main no longer creates repeated reapproval requests on a real iPhone across QR and manual setup, close without further code changes.

recommendation.title: Stabilize iOS approval declarations
recommendation.body: Keep reapproval for real new commands/capabilities while removing or normalizing volatile fields such as reachability/status from the approved node surface, with real iPhone reconnect proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this owner to the merged iOS LAN bootstrap repair and adjacent gateway/node-pairing reconciliation paths.
